newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zaire's Mobutu leaves Switzerland, officials say.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu leaves Switzerland, officials say.

text.p: Zaire's ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko left Switzerland on Monday on board a private plane for an unknown destination, Swiss Foreign Ministry and airport officials said.

A spokeswoman for the ministry in Berne told Reuters he had gone but could give no immediate details, and an official at Geneva's Cointrin airport said the Zairean leader flew out late in the afternoon.
The 66-year-old Mobutu, a one-time army sergeant who seized power in 1965, had been in Switzerland since August when he underwent surgery for prostate cancer at the University Hospital in Lausanne.

He had been living with his entourage of more than 20 bodyguards and aides at the city's luxury Beau-Rivage Palace hotel, but Swiss authorities were understood to have asked him to avoid public appearances or interviews.

His departure came as preparations were under way for a special United Nations envoy, Raymond Chretien, to visit him in Lausanne later this week to discuss the crisis in his country and the fighting in eastern Zaire.

Late last month, Swiss television reported that a villa owned by the reputedly super-rich Mobutu near Nice in the south of France was being prepared for his arrival. The report said he may continue his treatment there.
Last week former French internal affairs minister Charles Pasqua visited him in Lausanne.
